title: Deep merge
skill: Say what happens to each kind of value

good: Rewrite merge(target, source) in src/merge.js. Rules: 1) return a new object and never change target or source at any depth (tests freeze them); 2) a plain object (prototype is Object.prototype) in source merges recursively into the plain object at the same key; if the target value is not a plain object, merge into {}; 3) an array in source replaces the target value, no concat; 4) a source key whose value is undefined is skipped at every depth, and is not added to the result; 5) null overwrites; 6) every plain object and array in the result is a new copy at every depth, also the parts copied from target (arrays copied item by item, recursively); 7) other values (Date, Map, class instances) are kept by reference, not cloned or merged; 8) anything else from source replaces the target value. Do not change other files. Then run: node --test test/*.test.js
lazy: merge() in the config loader has bugs. Make it a proper deep merge.
